module_title: Grid Structure and Power System Faults
introduction: At this level, we cover the standard voltage backbone of the Indian grid, the types of insulators used, and the fundamental classification of short-circuit faults. These form the baseline of SSC JE preliminary exams.

core_concepts.title: Standard Voltages in India
core_concepts.description:
1. **Generation:** Typically done at 11 kV (sometimes up to 33 kV).
2. **Primary Transmission:** 400 kV, 220 kV, or 132 kV (for bulk power over long distances).
3. **Distribution:** Primary distribution at 11 kV, and Secondary distribution at 415 V (3-phase) or 240 V (single-phase domestic).

core_concepts.title: Power System Faults
core_concepts.description:
1. **Symmetrical Faults:** L-L-L or L-L-L-G faults. These are extremely **Rare** (only 2-5% of all faults) but are the **Most Severe / Dangerous** as all three phases are shorted together.
2. **Unsymmetrical Faults:** L-G, L-L, or L-L-G faults. 
- **L-G (Line to Ground) Fault:** This is the **Most Common** fault in a power system (accounting for 70-80% of all occurrences).

core_concepts.title: Overhead Line Insulators
core_concepts.description:
1. **Pin Type Insulator:** Economical and used strictly up to 33 kV.
2. **Suspension Type Insulator:** Used for voltages > 33 kV (e.g., 132 kV, 220 kV). Consists of a number of porcelain discs connected in series (each standard disc is designed to withstand 11 kV phase voltage).

important_entities.name: String Efficiency
important_entities.significance: In a suspension insulator string, the voltage is NOT distributed equally across all discs. The disc closest to the conductor experiences the maximum electrical stress. String efficiency measures how uniformly this voltage is distributed (closer to 100% is better).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Most Common vs. Most Severe Fault
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Exam Trap: Do not mix these up! 
- If asked 'Which is the most frequently occurring fault?' -> Answer: L-G (Line to Ground) fault. 
- If asked 'Which is the most severe/dangerous fault?' -> Answer: L-L-L (3-Phase) fault.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: One Disc per 11 kV of Phase Voltage
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If a line is 132 kV (Line-to-Line), Phase Voltage = 132 / 1.732 = approx 76 kV. Number of discs required = 76 / 11 = roughly 7 or 8 discs.

exam_strategy_tips: A patent SSC JE question: 'Up to what voltage is a pin-type insulator typically used?' Answer: 33 kV.
